title: From Hurt to Happiness: Emotional Rescue from the Ground Up
author: M. Murad Khan
target_audience: Individuals struggling with emotional pain or trauma
Adults seeking to improve emotional well-being
People interested in self-guided mental health strategies
Therapists and counselors seeking simple frameworks for clients
core_themes: Moving from emotional pain to happiness
Building resilience from the ground up
The importance of self-awareness and acceptance
primary_purpose: To provide readers with an accessible, step-by-step guide for overcoming emotional distress, fostering personal healing, and building a sustainable sense of happiness from within.

structure_format.organization: Structured progressively from understanding emotional pain to implementing habits of happiness, using clear steps and exercises

key_concepts_lessons: Hurt and happiness are two ends of an emotional spectrum that can be navigated.
Healing requires acknowledging and accepting painful emotions rather than avoiding them.
Small, grounded changes in daily habits can create significant emotional shifts.
Resilience is built by consistent self-care, mindfulness, and setting healthy boundaries.
True happiness comes from within and is accessible regardless of past hurts.
Emotional rescue is a gradual process involving patience, self-compassion, and actionable steps.
notable_features: Clear, practical frameworks for emotional self-care
Emphasis on starting from 'the ground up' with foundational habits
Integration of personal stories for relatability
Tools that can be self-applied without prior therapy experience
cultural_historical_context: Published during a period of increased global attention to mental health and emotional wellbeing, post-pandemic, when accessible self-help approaches have become more important and widely sought after.
reception_impact: Appreciated for its relatable language and actionable advice
Positive reviews from readers who found hope and clarity
Useful supplemental resource for therapy and counseling
Noted for its practicality in comparison to academic or overly-technical mental health books
comparable_titles: The Body Keeps the Score by Bessel van der Kolk
Permission to Feel by Marc Brackett
Emotional First Aid by Guy Winch
